gaps.sentence: She ___ on seeing the manager immediately.
gaps.explanation: Only 'insist' takes on + -ing; suggest and offer take bare -ing/to-infinitive respectively.

gaps.sentence: She ___ that the storm had passed.
gaps.explanation: Without a personal object, use said (that)...; told requires an object.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't forget your tickets,' she said to us. She ___ us to take our tickets.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't forget' maps onto remind + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: "We are leaving now." — They said they ___ then.
'I'll call you next week,' he promised. He promised he would call me ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' shifts to the following week (or the next week) from a later standpoint.

gaps.sentence: 'I moved here two years ago,' he explained. He explained that he had moved there two years ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Ago' becomes 'before' (or 'earlier') in reported speech; here → there as well.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll see you tomorrow,' he said. He said he would see me ___.
gaps.explanation: Time expressions shift: tomorrow becomes the next day / the following day.

gaps.sentence: 'Who broke the window?' the teacher demanded. The teacher demanded ___ the window.
gaps.explanation: 'Demand to know + wh-clause' with statement order; past simple backshifts to past perfect.
